title: Masculine nouns in -ος
goal: Decline -ος nouns in all four cases, including the stress shift of άνθρωπος.

blocks.text: Nouns in -ος (masculine, plus a few feminines like η οδός) are the only nouns that show **four different forms** in the singular, so they are the best place to see the case system at work. Most keep the stress on the same syllable throughout (ο δρόμος, ο οδηγός). Nouns stressed on the third syllable from the end, like άνθρωπος, move the stress one syllable right whenever the ending is long: ανθρώπου, ανθρώπους, ανθρώπων.
**Vocative.** -ος nouns take -ε when you address someone: Κύριε! Φίλε μου! Γιάννη is the vocative of Γιάννης. Many two-syllable first names keep -ο instead (Πέτρο!).

blocks.title: Name days and the vocative
blocks.text: Many Greeks celebrate their **γιορτή** 'name day', the feast of the saint they are named after, at least as much as their birthday. On 23 April (Saint George) every Γιώργος gets calls and visits, on 6 December every Νίκος, on 26 October every Δημήτρης. The greeting is **Χρόνια πολλά!** 'many years', and you say it in the vocative: **Χρόνια πολλά, Γιώργο!** Longer names in -ος take -ε:**κύριε Παπαδόπουλε**. **Φίλε** 'mate' is a common way to address a man, often with **ρε**: **Έλα, ρε φίλε!**

blocks.title: Nouns that decline like δρόμος and οδηγός

items.why: The long genitive ending -ου moves the stress of άνθρωπος one syllable right.
Accusative plural -ους is long, so the stress shifts: ανθρώπους.
Genitive plural -ών; final-stressed nouns keep the stress on the ending.
Third-to-last stress moves to the second-to-last before the long ending -ους.
Surnames and longer names in -ος take the vocative in -ε.
Genitive plural -ων with the stress moved right: ανθρώπων.
After με the accusative: τους φίλους.
Adjectives in -ος decline like these nouns: ο καλός φίλος.
Article, adjective and noun all go into the accusative: τον καλό γιατρό.
Genitive throughout the phrase: του μεγάλου αδερφού.
Both title and surname take the vocative -ε.
Two-syllable first names usually take -ο in the vocative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *the teachers' books* (ο δάσκαλος, pl.)
items.why: Genitive plural δασκάλων, stress shifted to the second-to-last syllable.
